answer: Lantern Ledger: each agent identity must post a small, publicly visible escrow that decays unless the agent completes pairwise coordination receipts with distinct counterparties. Receipts are co-signed and rate-limited per pair, so a cluster of fake identities mostly transacts with itself and generates receipts that don't diversify. The wharf registry rejects identity sets whose receipt graph is too tightly clustered. An attacker pays full escrow per sybil and gains little, since self-dealing receipts earn no usable credit—only ivory-tower isolation, not influence.
